summary: In Greek mythology, Asterius or Asterion (Ancient Greek Ἀστέριος / Ἀστερίων, "star-like" / "starry") is a name shared by many figures. The atlas node asterius-piresia is the Argonaut from Piresia (Peirasia) in Thessaly — son of Hyperasius (or of Cometes and Antigone daughter of Pheres) — paired in the catalogues with his brother Asterion/Amphion from the same Hyperasid house.

sections.heading: Thessalian Argonaut
paragraphs: Apollonius and Apollodorus count Asterius (Asterion) of Peirasia among the Argonauts, son of Hyperasius or of Cometes by Antigone of Pherae. He sails from the foot of Mount Phylleus as a catalogue companion rather than a solo episode hero.

Homonym guard: not Asterius/Asterion the Minotaur; not Asterion foster-father of Minos; not the Giant Asterius; not the Neleid prince slain by Heracles. Keep also distinct from asterion-pellene, the Pellenean Argonaut of the same Hyperasid naming cluster. The atlas id is the Piresian Argonaut alone.
